title: Chemistry 11 — Chapter 5: The Emissions Report
description: A furnace test burn, an oxide sample, and a spill neutralization all need to go in the same emissions report — and each one runs on a different kind of chemical process.

mika.name: Ms. Mika Tan
mika.description: Cares about environmental chemistry as much as the lab bench kind.

dev.name: Dev
dev.description: Knows combustion makes CO2 but not much past that.

combustion_notes.name: Combustion Notes
combustion_notes.description: Balancing rules for hydrocarbon combustion reactions.

oxide_chart.name: Oxide Behavior Chart
oxide_chart.description: Which oxides form acids and which form bases in water.

elements.text: Three processes to report on today: a furnace test burn, an oxide sample from the stack scrubber, and a spill that needs neutralizing. Different chemistry, same report.
Combustion just makes CO2, right? That part's easy.

elements.prompt: Mika hands you the combustion notes.

options.text: "CO2 and water, actually — and only if we balance it properly."

elements.text: Complete combustion of any hydrocarbon produces exactly two products: carbon dioxide and water. Methane's combustion is CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O — balance carbon first, then hydrogen, then oxygen last since it appears in both products.

config.question: What are the two products of complete combustion of any hydrocarbon?
config.explanation: Complete combustion (plenty of oxygen) always yields CO2 and H2O for a hydrocarbon.

config.prompt: The balanced equation is CH4 + __O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. What coefficient goes in front of O2?

elements.text: Metal oxides tend to react with water to form bases — calcium oxide plus water gives calcium hydroxide. Nonmetal oxides tend to form acids — carbon dioxide plus water gives carbonic acid. That difference is exactly why sulfur dioxide emissions matter.

config.prompt: Sort each oxide by what it forms when it reacts with water.

config.question: Sulfur dioxide reacting with atmospheric water vapor to form sulfurous and sulfuric acid is the main chemical cause of:
config.explanation: SO2 dissolving into atmospheric moisture and forming acidic compounds is the primary chemistry behind acid rain.

elements.text: There's an acid spill by the loading dock — what's the standard response?
Neutralize it: acid plus base always produces a salt and water. Hydrochloric acid plus sodium hydroxide gives sodium chloride and water — pH moves back toward neutral, and the hazard is gone.

config.prompt: HCl + NaOH -> ? Give the two products separated by a plus sign, no spaces (e.g. NaCl+H2O).

config.question: What are the two general products of any acid-base neutralization reaction?

options.text: Water only, with no other product

config.explanation: Neutralization always produces an ionic salt and water, regardless of which acid and base are involved.

elements.text: Combustion balanced, oxide behavior classified, spill neutralized correctly. The report is complete and accurate.
It's filed, but a couple of sections need a closer look. Let's revisit the oxide behavior before the next report.

elements.prompt: The report is ready to submit. What now?

options.text: Show Dev why sulfur dioxide emissions specifically matter, tying it back to the acid-forming chemistry.
File it and move on. Good enough for today.

elements.text: So combustion, oxides, and neutralization aren't three random topics — they're all just different reactions with predictable products once you know the pattern.

ending.title: Process Analyst
ending.description: Correctly balanced, classified, and explained all three chemical processes, and connected the oxide chemistry to real environmental impact.

ending.title: Report Filed
ending.description: The emissions report is complete and filed. The deeper environmental connection can wait.
